newsitem.title: CHINA: China tax revenue up 21.1 pct in Jan-Sept.
newsitem.headline: China tax revenue up 21.1 pct in Jan-Sept.

text.p: China collected 452.9 billion yuan in industrial and commercial taxes in the first nine months of this year, up 21.1 percent compared with the same 1995 period, the Xinhua news agency said.
The amount represented 75.1 percent of this year's target, Xinhua quoted Hao Zhaocheng, deputy director of the State Administration of Taxation, as saying in an overnight report.
A breakdown showed 249.8 billion yuan went into central government coffers, a year-on-year rise of 19.6 percent, he told a meeting on Monday.
The amount collected by local governments grew 22.9 percent to 203.1 billion yuan between January and September.
The consumption tax and the value-added tax, two major tax items under the new revenue-sharing taxation system introduced in 1994, came to 256.4 billion yuan, up 17.4 percent over a year ago.
Hao said problems still existed in taxation, citing tax evasion and other forms of cheating as the most serious.
Another outstanding problem was a time lag of 4.9 percent in collection of consumption tax and valued-added tax, Hao said.

He also cited a regional imbalance in the growth rate of tax collection, with the rate up by more than 25 percent in Shanghai, eastern Shandong province, southwestern Sichuan and another eight areas, but below five percent in southwestern Guangxi, western Qinghai, the northeastern city of Shenyang and southern Hainan.
Delayed tax payments rose by 16 billion yuan in the first nine months to 39.7 billion yuan by the end of September.
A national checkup on tax collection last year netted 16.577 billion yuan in sums evaded, in addition to 3.52 billion yuan in overdue taxes, Hao said.
